justification: Liability-sensitive surface (flood status figures) reaching two live report UIs. No DB/schema change and no backend change -- flood_studies has been on the wire since before this PR (both FloodServiceOutput and FloodDetail already declare it). This is purely wiring an already-served field into rendering that never consumed it, replacing a Hawkesbury-only special case with a generic one covering all four named studies. Standard, not critical: additive/generalizing only, every read defensively guards its own shape (matches the discipline established in the sibling in_100yr_flood_zone_unconsulted fix, PR #1061), and the old Hawkesbury path is kept as a fallback rather than deleted.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: before this change: FloodTool.tsx had 0 matches for flood_studies (only the hawkesbury_flood_level_* legacy fields were handled) and page.tsx had exactly 1 match (a FIELD_LABEL_OVERRIDES tooltip string, no render branch). After this change the counts are 5 and 2 respectively, reflecting the new type declaration/loop/render logic in each file. A regression that removes the new handling would drop these counts back toward 0/1.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Actually run in this session before writing the fix, not hypothetical: 'grep -n flood_studies frontend-nextjs/components/tools/FloodTool.tsx' returned zero matches (only hawkesbury_flood_level_* lines), and 'grep -n flood_studies\b page.tsx' returned exactly one line -- the FIELD_LABEL_OVERRIDES tooltip entry, no render branch. Confirmed the generic array formatter (formatValue, page.tsx:1775) would have rendered any object array as a bare 'N items' string, by reading its source directly rather than assuming.

pre_impl.existing_data: services/flood_truth.py already computes flood_studies (a list of {study_key, study_name, source, design, historical} dicts, one per matched named study) on every run, and both FloodServiceOutput and FloodDetail already declare the field -- confirmed by reading the models (no Python change needed here). /api/satellite/flood's route.ts spreads the full raw dict through untouched, so it already reaches FloodTool.tsx's JSON payload today; the Brief's typed pipeline already carries it to the rendered `data` prop.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: FloodTool.tsx's FloodOutputs interface never declared flood_studies, so its live depth-figure block only ever fired for the legacy hawkesbury_flood_level_* flat fields -- Redbank/Tweed/Wollongong's computed depth numbers were silently unused even when a raster matched. The Brief had zero special-case handling for flood_studies at all; it fell through to the generic array formatter (formatValue), which for an array of objects returns a bare 'N items' string with no figure -- confirmed by reading formatValue's array branch, not assumed.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future flood run that matches a named study with a readable 1% AEP raster. For FloodTool.tsx, the Hawkesbury-only fallback path is kept (only fires when the new generic loop didn't already cover 'hawkesbury'), so a genuinely old stored/paid report that predates flood_studies on the wire still renders exactly as it did before -- no regression for historical data.

functions.name: FloodCard's flood_studies loop
functions.input: the flood_studies array from the live API response, each element unknown at compile time
functions.output: one findings[] entry per study with a readable 1% AEP depth or level, or none
functions.if_none: empty/absent array, or every element missing a usable 1pct figure -> no entries pushed, falls through to the Hawkesbury-only fallback exactly as before this change

functions.name: SectionData flood_studies branch
functions.input: the raw val for this key from the untyped data bag, plus each study's design/1pct sub-object
functions.output: a row per named study with a figure, or null (nothing rendered) if no study yields a usable number
functions.if_none: not an array, empty array, or no study passes the studyName+onePct guard -> returns null, same silent nothing as before this change (previously rendered a useless 'N items' instead)

values.guard_at: both sites: typeof === 'number' check before use, plus a study-level continue/skip when neither figure is present
values.if_missing: that study is skipped (no row for it); other studies with a real figure still render

break_it.scenario: A flood_studies element has an unexpected shape (e.g. design is a string, or 1pct.depth_m is itself an object) due to a future backend refactor.
break_it.what_happens: Without defensive typing, this could throw (crashing the whole card) or render a bogus figure like '[object Object]m deep'.
break_it.how: Every level is guarded: `raw && typeof raw === 'object'`, `study.design && typeof study.design === 'object'`, `onePct && typeof onePct === 'object'`, and `typeof onePct.depth_m === 'number'` / `typeof onePct.level_m_ahd === 'number'` before ever touching .toLocaleString(). A failing guard skips that one study rather than throwing or rendering garbage.
break_it.repro: Manual: construct a flood_studies fixture with design: 'not an object' or design: {'1pct': {depth_m: {}}} and confirm the study is silently skipped, not rendered or thrown.

break_it.scenario: Duplicate rendering: a Hawkesbury address matches the new generic flood_studies loop AND the old flat hawkesbury_flood_level_100aep fallback, producing two rows for the same study.
break_it.what_happens: Redundant/confusing duplicate flood-depth rows for the same address.
break_it.how: FloodTool.tsx:630 -- studiesShown tracks study_key values the generic loop already rendered; the legacy fallback is gated on `!studiesShown.has('hawkesbury')`, so it only fires when the generic loop did NOT already cover Hawkesbury (i.e. genuinely old data missing flood_studies).
break_it.repro: Manual: construct a fixture where flood_studies contains a hawkesbury entry with a 1pct figure AND hawkesbury_flood_level_100aep is also set; confirm only one '1-in-100-year' row renders, not two.

break_it.scenario: The Brief's flood_studies branch previously fell through to the generic array formatter (formatValue), which is not a crash but is a real regression risk if the new branch is ever removed without checking what formatValue does with an object array.
break_it.what_happens: Silently reverting to a useless 'N items' label with no figure, easy to miss since it's not an error.
break_it.how: Documented explicitly in the new branch's comment (page.tsx:773-774) and in this QA report's pre_impl section, so a future editor sees the fallback behaviour named rather than rediscovering it via formatValue's source.
break_it.repro: Read frontend-nextjs/lib or the inline formatValue function at page.tsx:1775 -- the Array.isArray branch's non-primitive case returns `${val.length} item(s)`.

break_it.scenario: Sol cross-review (3 x MEDIUM, 0.99/0.98/0.9) on the first push: (a) the finding label always said 'flood depth' even when a study supplied only level_m_ahd and no depth_m, misrepresenting a level as a depth; (b) the detail text made an unsupported universal claim ('your insurer and lender both use figures like this') about third parties' behaviour; (c) Hawkesbury deduplication depended solely on an exact study_key === 'hawkesbury' match, so a malformed/differently-cased key on a genuine Hawkesbury entry would let the same study render twice (generic row + legacy fallback row).
break_it.what_happens: (a) reader sees a mislabeled figure; (b) an overclaimed statement about third-party underwriting practice; (c) a confusing duplicate flood-depth row for the same address.
break_it.how: FloodTool.tsx:667-683 -- label now derives from which measurement is actually present (depth vs level); the insurer/lender sentence softened to 'may use... confirm their specific requirements directly' in both the generic loop and the legacy fallback; Hawkesbury dedup now checks a lowercased study_key OR a case-insensitive study_name match, not the key alone. NOTE: the same unqualified insurer/lender claim pattern pre-exists elsewhere in this file (lines 351-365, 581, 588) — untouched, out of scope for this PR (not part of the diff Sol reviewed), flagged here for a future pass rather than silently left unnoticed.
break_it.repro: Manual: construct a fixture with design['1pct'] = {level_m_ahd: 12.34, depth_m: null} and confirm the label reads '...flood level', not '...flood depth'; construct a fixture with a Hawkesbury study_name but study_key: 'Hawkesbury ' (trailing space/different case) plus hawkesbury_flood_level_100aep set, and confirm only one row renders.

post_merge.manual_verify: On the deployed preview, run a flood check for an address in the Redbank, Tweed, or Wollongong LGA where the study raster covers the point, and confirm both /reports/flood and the Intelligence Brief now show a real '1-in-100-year flood depth' figure (not just a plain yes/no), matching what a Hawkesbury address already showed before this PR.
